findings.claim: _create_proposal_branch runs git checkout -b which permanently switches the repository HEAD to the proposal branch; subsequent propose() calls in the same server session create branches from the proposal branch instead of the original working base; no HEAD restoration occurs after propose_impl returns.
findings.evidence: tools.py:554-563 — _create_proposal_branch executes git checkout -b branch_name (not git branch branch_name). git checkout -b creates AND switches HEAD. After propose_impl returns at line 862, the repo HEAD is on scp-mcp-proposal/prop-NNN with no restoration. test_propose.py:44 explicitly asserts current_branch == response.branch_name, confirming the branch switch is observed. For a second distinct propose() call in the same session: _next_proposal_id returns PROP-002; _create_proposal_branch runs git checkout -b scp-mcp-proposal/prop-002 while HEAD is on prop-001; git creates prop-002 based at the HEAD of prop-001, not at the original working branch. test_propose_serialises_distinct_concurrent_submissions at test_propose.py:135-165 monkeypatches _create_proposal_branch to a no-op, so the chaining is never exercised in the test suite.
findings.impact: First, proposal branches form a chain from each other rather than a fan-out from the working base. When 021E makes a commit to a proposal branch, subsequent proposal branches will inherit that commit (since each branches from the previous). Second, any audit_changed call with symbolic refs (HEAD, HEAD~1) after propose() resolves against the proposal branch; currently benign since no commits are made to proposal branches, but will produce incorrect diffs once 021E lands. Third, the running server's git working context is permanently altered; operators have no indication that HEAD has been switched and no automated path to restore it. WP-SCP-021 §2 invariant 'writes only to branches, never to main' is satisfied in the letter but the spirit — proposal branches origin from a stable reference — is violated for all proposals after the first.
findings.mitigation: Replace git checkout -b with git branch <branch_name> to create the branch without switching HEAD. Also add an assertion that both branches share the same parent commit.

If the write fails (FileExistsError from a cross-process race past the flock guard, OSError from ENOSPC/EROFS, or SIGKILL between branch creation and file creation), lines 859-861 return _error('SCP-MCP-E021', ...) with no cleanup. The branch scp-mcp-proposal/prop-NNN remains in git. On retry: _next_proposal_id (line 829) scans PROP-*.md; since PROP-NNN.md does not exist it returns the same NNN; _create_proposal_branch fails with 'a branch named scp-mcp-proposal/prop-NNN already exists'; propose() returns E021 permanently for all subsequent calls with any content, since every new proposal attempts NNN and is blocked. test_propose_does_not_write_file_when_branch_creation_fails (test_propose.py:48) only tests the branch-failure path, not the file-failure-after-branch-success path.
findings.impact: Any OS error during file write, or a SIGKILL between branch creation and file write, permanently blocks the propose() ID slot. All future proposals will attempt the same NNN (no file exists) and fail at branch creation. The only recovery is manual: git branch -D scp-mcp-proposal/prop-NNN and git checkout <original_branch>. This creates a permanent DoS of the propose() tool for any subsequent proposal in the session. Violates the 'clean completion' guarantee implied by the dispatch AC: 'Writes a new file at docs/reviews/proposals/PROP-NNN.md on a feature branch' — branch and file must be co-present or both absent.
findings.mitigation: Before calling _create_proposal_branch, record the current branch via git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD. Wrap _write_new_proposal_file in a try/except that, on failure: (1) deletes the created branch via git branch -D branch_name, (2) restores HEAD to the original branch via git checkout <original_branch>, and (3) returns the structured error. Alternatively, write the file first using O_EXCL (file creation is the atomic claim); only call _create_proposal_branch after successful file creation; on branch-creation failure, unlink the file via os.unlink(proposal_path) and return E021. Add a test that monkeypatches _write_new_proposal_file to raise OSError and asserts (a) no branch remains in the repo and (b) HEAD is restored to the original branch.

findings.claim: audit_changed_impl passes the original symbolic ref strings (base_ref, head_ref) to _list_changed_files_with_timeout and _run_audit_changed_cli after resolving those refs to SHAs for the cache key; a TOCTOU window exists between SHA resolution and diff execution where HEAD can change, causing the diff to run on a different object than the cache key recorded.
findings.evidence: tools.py:745-760 — _resolve_git_commit resolves both refs to SHAs; _audit_cache_key(resolved_base_ref, resolved_head_ref) at line 760 correctly keys on SHAs. tools.py:767-771 — _list_changed_files_with_timeout(base_ref=base_ref, head_ref=head_ref, ...) uses original symbolic refs. tools.py:787-791 — _run_audit_changed_cli(base_ref=base_ref, head_ref=head_ref, ...) uses original symbolic refs. If propose() (which calls git checkout -b, switching HEAD) runs concurrently or if HEAD advances due to an external commit between lines 754 and 767, git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD (inside _list_changed_files_with_timeout) resolves HEAD to a new SHA. The cache entry is stored under the pre-call SHA key; the result reflects the post-call HEAD. For stdio mode this is benign (no concurrent writes). For HTTP mode (021H) or after 021E commits to proposal branches, the window is exploitable.
findings.impact: When HEAD changes between SHA resolution and diff execution, the audit result cached under the pre-call SHA reflects changes in the post-call HEAD's diff. A caller who receives the result from the resolved SHA may believe they are seeing the audit for the pre-call state; they are actually seeing the post-call state. Cache invalidation is also broken: the same resolved SHA is looked up on the next call and returns the result that was computed for a different HEAD state. Low impact in current 021C stdio mode; becomes a correctness regression when 021E commits and propose() switches branches in the same session.
findings.mitigation: Pass resolved_base_ref and resolved_head_ref to _list_changed_files_with_timeout and _run_audit_changed_cli instead of the original symbolic ref strings. This eliminates the TOCTOU window: the same git objects are used for cache key computation and for diff execution. Update _run_audit_changed_cli to pass the resolved SHAs as --base-ref and --head-ref arguments to the CLI subprocess, ensuring the audit CLI also operates on the pinned objects.

findings.claim: _PROPOSAL_NORMALISATION_PATTERN does not cover Unicode bidi control characters U+202A-U+202E (LRE, RLE, PDF, LRO, RLO); an attacker can embed RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE (U+202E) or other bidi controls in a proposal to bypass the SCP-MCP-E020 duplicate detection gate, which was the stated target of SR-SAFE-002.
findings.evidence: tools.py:48 — _PROPOSAL_NORMALISATION_PATTERN = re.compile(r'[\s\u200b-\u200f\u2028\u2029\ufeff]+', re.UNICODE). Range \u200b-\u200f covers U+200B through U+200F only; U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE is at U+202E, outside this range and not individually listed. \s with re.UNICODE matches Unicode category Z (separators) and standard ASCII whitespace per CPython 3.x documentation; category Cf (format characters, which includes U+202A-U+202E) is excluded. unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', combined) at line 509 does not decompose or remove Cf-category bidi controls. SR-SAFE-002 R1 mitigation text (consolidation-r1.json line 92) explicitly listed 'U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE' as a target character. test_propose_rejects_duplicate_with_invisible_unicode at test_propose.py:94-117 uses U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR, covered) and U+200E (LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK, covered by \u200b-\u200f) but does not test U+202E or any U+202A-U+202E range character.
findings.impact: An adversary can submit a proposal with title 'Add MCP policy' body 'Queue this.', then re-submit with title 'Add MCP‮policy' (U+202E inserted). The normalized hashes differ; _existing_proposal_hashes returns no match; a new PROP-NNN file is created without triggering SCP-MCP-E020. The proposals_root directory can be flooded with visually identical proposals differing only in invisible bidi controls. SR-SAFE-002 is only partially closed.
findings.mitigation: Extend _PROPOSAL_NORMALISATION_PATTERN to include U+202A-U+202E (bidi embedding/override controls) and U+2060-U+206F (invisible math operators and deprecated format chars): re.compile(r'[\s\u200b-\u200f\u2028\u2029\ufeff\u202a-\u202e\u2060-\u206f]+', re.UNICODE). Alternatively, strip all Unicode category Cf characters before normalisation: ''.join(c for c in text if unicodedata.category(c) != 'Cf'). Add a test asserting that a proposal with an embedded U+202E is rejected as a duplicate of the same proposal without U+202E.

findings.claim: _parse_decisions_table uses re.fullmatch(r'D-\d{3}', cells[0]) which silently drops decision IDs with four or more digits (D-1000 and above); list_open_decisions will return a truncated list once the decision log reaches D-1000 with no error or warning.
findings.evidence: tools.py:354 — re.fullmatch(r'D-\d{3}', cells[0]). Contrast with _PROPOSAL_ID_PATTERN at line 46: r'^PROP-(\d{3,})\.md$' which uses {3,}. The decision log will reach D-1000 at the current assignment rate. Not fixed in fix-round-1. Carry-forward from R1 COR-006.
findings.impact: list_open_decisions silently omits any decision at or above D-1000. The caller receives a truncated list indistinguishable from a complete one. Silent data loss.
findings.mitigation: Change tools.py:354 to re.fullmatch(r'D-\d{3,}', cells[0]) to match 3 or more digits, consistent with _PROPOSAL_ID_PATTERN.

findings.claim: check_waiver_impl scope filter incorrectly excludes global waivers (area_id=None) when a non-None scope is requested, causing active globally-scoped waivers to be silently omitted from the response.
findings.evidence: tools.py:641-642 — if request.scope is not None and finding.get('area_id') != request.scope: continue. When a finding has no area_id (area_id=None), finding.get('area_id') returns None; None != request.scope evaluates True for any non-None scope string, so the global waiver is skipped. No test covers the global-finding + scoped-request combination. Carry-forward from R1 COR-007.
findings.impact: A caller asking 'are there active waivers for rule ARCH-001 in scope returns-exceptions?' misses any globally-scoped waivers for ARCH-001 (those with no area_id). The consumer may incorrectly treat a globally-waived finding as unwaived, potentially re-opening a finding that was intentionally globally exempted.
findings.mitigation: Change the guard at tools.py:641 to: if request.scope is not None and finding.get('area_id') is not None and finding.get('area_id') != request.scope: continue. This allows findings with area_id=None (global scope) to match any scope request. Add a test with a global finding (area_id absent) and a scoped request asserting the waiver is returned.

structured_review.fixpoint_rationale: All 11 R1 CRIT+MAJ findings are verified closed under the correctness lens. Two new MAJ findings are identified in R2: COR-R2-001 (git checkout -b permanently mutates repo HEAD, causing proposal branch chaining in a single session with no restoration) and COR-R2-002 (no rollback on partial failure after branch creation, creating a permanent stuck state). Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3, new MAJ findings raised by any R2 reviewer block fixpoint. The slice requires a fix-round-2 addressing COR-R2-001 and COR-R2-002 before the correctness lens can declare fixpoint. Four MIN findings remain open (COR-R2-003, COR-R2-004 as new, COR-006 and COR-007 as carry-forward) but do not individually block fixpoint.

structured_review.summary: R2 correctness review of slice 021C after fix-round-1. All 11 R1 CRIT+MAJ closures verified. Two new MAJ findings identified: (1) propose() uses git checkout -b which permanently switches HEAD to the proposal branch with no restoration, causing branch chaining for multiple proposals in one session; (2) no rollback when file write fails after branch creation, permanently blocking that proposal ID slot. Two new MIN findings: TOCTOU between SHA resolution and symbolic-ref usage in git diff; bidi control chars U+202A-U+202E not covered by the duplicate-gate normalisation. Two MIN carry-forwards: D-\d{3} regex drops D-1000+; global waivers incorrectly excluded on scoped requests. Fixpoint NOT_REACHED.
